title: The Heavy box on the cart
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（科学与技术·工程与建造）　|　核心词汇：heavy　|　正文 334 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 heavy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1985 the father wrote of ① a heavy box on the cart in the letter, and everybody in the house said at once that it was ② heavier than the one named there the year before. Three months on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the father, who never explained anything, had done it at once and gone home; it was the heavy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the heaviest box on the cart anybody in the house had ever seen, or so the letter for September 1979 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too heavy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the neighbour who had come to help; the heavy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the chair at the far door, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a heavy load of work, and said that no neighbour in his right mind would call it ⑥ as heavy as the load of work they had once had in the old house. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was heavy or not, and he said so.

By 1992 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the letter. What the line asked for was ⑦ something heavy, and nothing besides. The neighbour from the next house called the whole plan ⑧ quite heavy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the letter kept the names of the heavy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1995, in the rain, she wrote of another heavy box on the cart in the same letter, and the work, which took two months, seemed ⑨ heavier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The heaviest load of work in the whole house, she said in 1997, was the one she could never quite name; the heavy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 重（前置定语 a heavy box on the cart：1985 年父亲在家书里记下的那件重的箱子）
B. adj. 重／繁重（比较级 heavier than：文中两处，一处比车上的重箱子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 重／繁重（最高级 the heaviest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 重（表语 too heavy to do：母亲觉得它太重，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 繁重（前置定语 a heavy load of work：叔叔把整件事称作一桩繁重的工作负担）
F. adj. 繁重（同级比较 as heavy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩繁重的工作负担相比）
G. adj. 繁重（后置定语 something heavy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 繁重（受程度副词修饰 quite heavy：那位邻居的评价）

items.q: a heavy box on the cart
the heaviest box on the cart anybody
The heaviest load of work in

answers.why: heavy 意为“重”，1985 年父亲在家书里记下的是“一件重的箱子”，此处作前置定语 a heavy box on the cart。
heavy 意为“重”，此处用比较级 heavier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
heavy 意为“重”，家书上 九月 那行字说它是老屋里最重的一件，故用最高级 the heaviest box on the cart。
heavy 意为“重”，母亲认为这件东西“太重了，谁也用不上”，too heavy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
heavy 意为“繁重”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩繁重的工作负担”，此处作前置定语 a heavy load of work。
heavy 意为“繁重”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩繁重的工作负担一样繁重”，同级比较用 as heavy as。
heavy 意为“繁重”，家书上那半行字要的是“繁重的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something heavy。
heavy 意为“繁重”，邻老屋来的那位邻居认为这套计划“相当繁重”，quite 修饰原级 heavy。
heavy 意为“繁重”，1995 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要繁重”，故用比较级 heavier than。
heavy 意为“繁重”，母亲 1997 年说的是“整个老屋里最繁重的那一桩”，故用最高级 the heaviest load of work。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1985 年，父亲在家书里记下了一件重的箱子。（a heavy box on the cart）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更重。（heavier than …）
母亲觉得它太重，谁也用不上。（too heavy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩繁重的工作负担。（a heavy load of work）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩繁重的工作负担一样繁重。（as heavy as …）
到了 1992 年，家书上只剩半行字：要的是一件繁重的东西。（something heavy）
answers: In 1985 the father wrote of a heavy box on the cart in the letter.
Everybody said it was heavier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too heavy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a heavy load of work.
He said nobody would call it as heavy as the load of work they had once had.
By 1992 the letter asked for nothing but something heavy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 heavy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1985 the father wrote of a heavy box on the cart in the letter, and nobody forgot it.
It was the heaviest box on the cart in the house, or so the letter says.
My mother thought it too heavy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a heavy load of work, and nobody argued with him.
The neighbour from the next house called the plan quite heavy, and everybody laughed.
The heavy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
